text:
maya: Hey team — ACME Inc ran into a card decline while upgrading to Dedicated. Customer says card works elsewhere. Billing logs show AVS + CVV failures. Can we confirm next steps?

chris: Can you paste the gateway response + transaction id and how many attempts?

maya: Sure, here are the details from our payment gateway:```
txn_id: tx_6f3b9a7c
status: decline
decline_code: card_declined
avs_result: N (address does not match)
cvv_result: N (cvv incorrect)
processor_response: "AVS/CVV mismatch - address zip doesn't match issuer record"
processor: stripe
amount: $1,200.00
customer_email: billing@acme-inc.com
attempts: 2
card_brand: Visa
last4: 4242
```

sophie: AVS=N and CVV=N — that's a classic cardholder verification failure. Two possibilities: billing address formatting (PO BOX vs street, suite vs #) or the issuer is blocking merchant category. Do we have the exact billing address on file and what the customer typed at the bank?

maya: Customer says their billing address is "PO Box 4321" at the bank, but in our billing profile they entered the street address. They tried updating to PO Box and retried, still declined. They also tried calling their bank and they said there's a "cardholder verification flag" on the token.

liam: From finance side — if the customer can provide a PO number we can do a manual invoice (net30) and skip the card. Otherwise the fastest path is a new card or ACH. We can also start a vendor onboarding for ACME if they expect recurring purchases via PO.

chris: We should avoid recharging multiple times; processors will auto-block after repeated CVV fails. Don't retry more than once without explicit customer consent. Maya — did they consent to the retry?

maya: They consented to one retry and it failed. They asked if we can force-charge or white-list their attempts.

sophie: We can't white-list on the processor side — the issuer decides CVV/AVS checks. Forcing a charge without cardholder auth is not allowed. Technical mitigation: ensure AVS fields match exactly what the issuer has (including punctuation and abbreviations). If they used PO BOX, that must match bank record. Also try a different card brand or card on file.

liam: If they provide a PO we need: PO number, billing contact, legal name and billing address. Once we have that finance can issue an invoice and mark it for immediate provisioning if approved. If they want immediate access today, they should provide an alternate payment method.

maya: Customer asked for a checklist to unblock quickly. I told them: 1) Confirm exact billing address with bank (match punctuation), 2) Try alternate card or ACH, 3) If they can provide a PO we can invoice them (send to finance@redwood.com).

chris: Also record the decline code and attach the gateway logs to the support ticket. I'll tag this high-priority until payment confirmed.

billing-bot: Automated: Payment attempt failed for tx_6f3b9a7c (amount $1,200.00). Support ticket created: #4582. Customer notified by email.

maya: Customer replied: they'll try their company card after confirming address with the bank, and will send a PO if the retry fails. I'll keep the thread updated.

liam: If PO comes in, please include requested billing contact and whether they need supplier onboarding. I'll take ownership of invoices once we have PO.

chris: Thanks — one more note for the record: if AVS=N and CVV=N and the customer reports the card works elsewhere, recommend they ask their issuing bank to lift cardholder verification blocks or to allow one-off merchant. Banks sometimes block e-commerce merchants for MCC mismatch.

maya: Got it. Marking as ongoing; will update ticket #4582 with finance contact. :thumbsup:

chris: Thanks Maya. If it becomes recurring pattern across accounts we should flag for payments ops to consider alternate processors or explicit guidance in billing docs.

maya: Will do. Closing slack thread for now, will reopen if we get more declines from ACME.
